segments.text: If you were born on the ninth, the eighteenth, or the twenty-seventh, this is your number. Moolank nine.
Your ruling planet is Mars, and your element is fire. That is why your energy never seems to run out.
segments.caption: Planet: Mars · Element: Fire

segments.text: Courage, and a sense of justice so strong that you take a stand and you hold it.
segments.caption: Courage. Justice. You hold your ground.

segments.text: But fire with no direction turns into friction.
segments.caption: Fire with no direction turns to friction.

segments.text: Lucky numbers three, six and nine. Colour red. Day Tuesday.
segments.caption: 3 · 6 · 9   |   Red   |   Tuesday

segments.text: Your daily remedy. Chant Om Angarakaya Namah. Read the Hanuman Chalisa, and donate blood. It cools the anger, and turns restless fire into courage.
segments.caption: ॐ अंगारकाय नमः

_comment: Narration for the animated card reels. ⭐⭐⭐ EVERYTHING IS ENGLISH, EVERYWHERE (owner's standing decision, 2026-08-05). Two reasons, and the second is the one that binds: a reel goes out on all four platforms so one language reads as one voice across them, AND every language variant of the same number is a SECOND ElevenLabs generation off a finite balance. Write each number once, in English. 🪤 The saving is in the RE-narration, not the language — ElevenLabs bills per character either way, and this script is ~495 characters, so a number costs ~500 credits however it is written. Regenerating one number in a second language is what actually doubles the bill. So: do not add a Hinglish variant of a number that already exists, and do not re-run `narration --force` to try a phrasing you have not read aloud to yourself first. ⭐ ENGLISH NEEDS NO DEVANAGARI, BUT IT STILL NEEDS SPELLED-OUT NUMERALS: write "the ninth, the eighteenth", not "the 9th, the 18th". A bare digit is where the model's reading is least predictable, and the date list IS the hook — every qualifying date must be named or the audience that self-identifies shrinks to a quarter (confirmed 3x). ⭐ The HINGLISH rules are kept only for the record, in case the decision is ever revisited: write the Hindi in Devanagari and leave English words in Latin, because Latin-transliterated Hindi makes the model guess (it stuttered a-agar, split ni-ne, stretched mangaaal). `language` records what a reel actually is; it is "en" on everything now. `narrate:false` keeps a field on the card but out of the voiceover; `caption` is reference copy for hand-posting, the render reads its text from moolank-cards.json. 🪤 Do NOT use the ॐ glyph in narration TEXT in any language - the model spells it out letter by letter as A-U-M. The glyph is fine ON SCREEN, just not in what gets spoken.
